implementation_notes: Ruby is dynamically typed, so the newtype is an ordinary class and the only enforcement is the object's own interface: Data.define(:value) creates an immutable, value-equal class in one line - reader, positional and keyword constructor, ==/eql?/hash and deconstruct come from the stdlib, and members have no writers. On older Rubies the same shape is a hand-written class that freezes its instances and defines ==, eql? and hash (include Comparable only when ordering is part of the domain). Since nothing stops a raw String from reaching a method that expects the wrapper, provide one explicit parse/from conversion and keep the raw accessor read-only.
code_sketch:
Measure = Data.define(:value) do
  def self.parse(raw)
    raise ArgumentError, "empty amount" if raw.to_s.empty?
    new(raw)
  end
end

distance = Measure.parse(100)
pitfalls: Data gives value semantics but not deep immutability: a mutable member object can still be mutated, so freeze or wrap only primitive payloads.
Equality must be defined as a set: a wrapper that overrides == without eql?/hash is unusable as a Hash key - use Data.define (which defines all three) rather than an ad-hoc class.

Duck typing means an unwrapped String still flows into any method that does not check the class, so the guarantee is a convention plus is_a? checks; avoid to_str/to_int-style implicit conversions that re-admit the primitive.
